text: Sodium acetate. The sodium ion is a spectator. But acetate is the conjugate base of a weak acid, so it pulls a proton off a water molecule, forming acetic acid and leaving a hydroxide ion behind. The solution turns alkaline. This is anionic hydrolysis.
